tasks.title: M0.1 Measure slot save, restore and re-prefill on the brain
tasks.description:
Goal: numbers for how long it takes to save and restore a llama.cpp slot, and how fast the brain re-reads a prompt, so later cards can choose thresholds.

Do: write scripts/measure_slots.sh, modelled on scripts/engine-try.sh (which already times a save and a restore on a small model). Against the live brain at http://127.0.0.1:11434, for prompt sizes of about 8000, 32000 and 100000 tokens: (1) send the prompt to slot 0 with "id_slot":0 and "cache_prompt":true and max_tokens 1; record prompt tokens and seconds (this is re-prefill speed, tokens per second). (2) POST /slots/0?action=save with {"filename":"measure-<size>.bin"}; record seconds and the file size in /var/lib/jarvis/slots. (3) POST /slots/0?action=erase, then action=restore with the same filename; record seconds. (4) Repeat steps 2-3 once with the snapshot file copied to a tmpfs directory to see if RAM is faster to read (if the engine can only read its --slot-save-path, say so and skip). Delete the measure-*.bin files at the end.

Write the results to docs/runtime/measurements.md under a heading '## Save, restore, re-prefill' as one table: size, snapshot MB, save s, restore s, re-prefill tokens/s. Under it write one line starting 'snapshot_min_tokens:' with the prompt size below which re-prefill is faster than save plus restore.

Run it only when no agent job is running (jarvis-jobs show; nothing in status running on driver local).

Rules: this card runs on the sonnet driver. Never run it from a local round. Open a maintenance window first (jarvis-watchdog maintain 2h) if the card stops or loads the brain, and leave the brain running and healthy when you finish.
tasks.acceptance_check: bash -n scripts/measure_slots.sh && grep -q '^snapshot_min_tokens:' docs/runtime/measurements.md

tasks.title: M1.2e Checkpoint and RecoverLoop: make the tests pass
tasks.description:
Goal: implement Store.Checkpoint and Store.RecoverLoop so the tests from card m1-2d pass.

1. s.AppendMessages(id, cp.Messages...). If failAfter == 1, return errInjected.
2. For each op in cp.Ops: s.PutOp(id, op). If failAfter == 2, return errInjected.
3. Write the state with the store's existing state setter (s.SetStatus(id, cp.State)).

4. Count tool calls that have a later message with Role "tool" whose Content has "tool_call_id" equal to the call's ID; those are answered.
5. Read the job. Only change the state when Status is "running" or "waiting": if there are unanswered tool calls set Status "waiting" and WaitReason WaitOperation; if there are none set Status "ready" and clear WaitReason. Do not write when nothing changes.

tasks.description:
Goal: one pure function that says what a job's status becomes when an event arrives. No I/O, no store, no broker.

Do: create runtime/lifecycle/lifecycle.go, package lifecycle. Import github.com/ImMakingAJarvis/ai-agent-build/internal/agentjob only for the wait-reason constants and github.com/ImMakingAJarvis/ai-agent-build/internal/queue for the event type constants.
type In struct { Status, WaitReason string; Event string; OpenOps int; OpenChildren int; ModelSuspended bool }   // OpenOps = operations of the job that are not finished AFTER this event is applied
type Out struct { Status, WaitReason string; Changed bool }
func Transition(in In) Out
Use the status strings the store already uses; read internal/agentjob/store.go for the constants (ready, running, waiting, done, failed and the stopped/parked one). Rules, in this order:
1. A finished job (done, failed, stopped/parked) never changes: Changed false.
2. Event cancel.requested: status becomes the store's stopped/parked status, reason "".
3. Event model.suspended and status ready or waiting: waiting, reason model.
4. Event model.resumed and reason model: if OpenOps > 0 then waiting/operation; else if OpenChildren > 0 then waiting/child; else ready.
5. Event op.done, approval.decided or task.done (a child finished), and status waiting: if ModelSuspended then waiting/model; else if OpenOps > 0 keep waiting/operation; else if OpenChildren > 0 waiting/child; else ready with reason "".
6. Event user.message and status waiting with reason user: ready.
7. Anything else: unchanged, Changed false.

tasks.description:
Goal: implement runtime/slot so the tests from card m2-3a pass. Do not change the tests except to delete the t.Skip lines.

The Manager keeps, under one sync.Mutex, for each slot: holder (job id currently RUNNING a tick in it, "" if none), warm (job id whose KV is in the slot, "" if none), tokens, and lastReleased (a counter that increases on every Release; use a counter, not time).

Acquire(ctx, jobID), in this order:
1. If some slot has warm == jobID and holder == "": take it. Lease{Warm: true}. No engine calls.
2. Else pick a slot with holder == "" and warm == "" (lowest number first).
3. Else pick, among slots with holder == "", the one with the smallest lastReleased. If there is none, return ErrNoSlot. Evict its warm job W: if the slot's tokens >= cfg.SnapshotMinTokens then info := eng.Info(ctx); eng.SaveSlot(ctx, slot, W+".bin"); jobs.SetSnapshot(W, W+".bin", info.Fingerprint(), tokens). In both cases jobs.SetWarmSlot(W, nil) and clear the slot's warm.
4. For a slot taken in step 2 or 3: js := jobs.Get(jobID). If js.Snapshot != "": if js.SnapshotFingerprint == eng.Info(ctx).Fingerprint() then eng.RestoreSlot(ctx, slot, js.Snapshot) and Lease.Restored = true; otherwise jobs.SetSnapshot(jobID, "", "", 0) (the snapshot is stale; the tick will re-read the prompt). If there was no snapshot and the slot was evicted in step 3, call eng.EraseSlot(ctx, slot).
5. Set holder = jobID, warm = jobID, jobs.SetWarmSlot(jobID, &slot). Return the lease.
An engine or jobs error returns the error and leaves the slot with holder == "".
Release(l, tokens): holder = "", tokens = tokens, lastReleased = next counter value. The job stays warm.
Forget(jobID): clear warm for that job in every slot where holder == "".
Warm(): a copy of slot -> warm job id for slots where warm != "".

Do the engine calls while holding the mutex (simple and correct; ticks are long, acquires are rare).

tasks.description:

type BlockEdit struct { Path, Old, New string }
func ParseBlockEdits(text string) ([]BlockEdit, error)
Format, one or more blocks:
<path on its own line>
<<<<<<< SEARCH
<old lines>
=======
<new lines>
>>>>>>> REPLACE
The path is the last non-empty line before the SEARCH marker; strip backticks and spaces around it. An empty SEARCH part means "create the file with the REPLACE part". A SEARCH marker with no ======= or no REPLACE marker is an error naming the block number.

tasks.title: B1 Benchmark suite: six fixed jobs, three scenarios, one script
tasks.description:
Goal: a fixed benchmark we can run before and after each milestone, to see whether the runtime is actually better than Claude Code rounds on the local brain. Nothing here depends on the runtime; it must run today.

Do:
1. Fixtures under docs/runtime/bench/fixtures/, each a tiny self-contained directory with its own check command:
 - edit-small: a Go module with one failing test; the job fixes one function. Check: go test ./...
 - slow-test: the same kind of bug, but the test suite takes about 60 s (a sleep in TestMain). Check: go test ./...
 - slow-command: the job must run './fetch.sh' (which sleeps 120 s and then writes data.txt) and then write the number of lines of data.txt into answer.txt. Check: test "$(cat answer.txt)" = "$(wc -l < data.txt | tr -d ' ')"
 - multi-file: rename a function used in five files. Check: go build ./... && ! grep -rn OldName .
 - big-log: './build.sh' prints about 200 KB of log with ONE real error line in the middle; the job fixes the cause. Check: ./build.sh
 - docs: write a README section describing the three exported functions of a small package. Check: grep -c for the three names in README.md equals 3.
2. docs/runtime/bench/suite.json: for each job its id, instructions (plain words, the same text for every driver), fixture directory and check command; and three scenarios: S1 = each job alone, one after another; S2 = all six queued at the same moment; S3 = S2 plus five chat messages sent 60 s apart while it runs.
3. scripts/bench_runtime.sh <driver> <scenario> <out.json>: copies the fixtures to a fresh temp workspace, creates the jobs for that driver (read docs/agent-run.md and cmd/jarvis-jobs for how to add and run a job on a named driver without the Discord checkpoint), waits for them, runs each check, and writes out.json with, per job: status, check passed, wall seconds, kWh from the job store; and for the whole run: wall seconds, jobs passed, GPU utilisation average and VRAM peak (Prometheus at :9090, the nvidia exporter metrics), prompt and generated tokens (difference of the llamacpp counters on the engine's /metrics before and after), seconds the GPU was under 10 percent busy while a job was unfinished, and for S3 the reply time of each chat message. Tag every job 'bench'.
4. scripts/bench_runtime_test.sh: runs the script with driver 'fake' (a mode that marks jobs done without a model) to prove the collection and the JSON shape work.
5. docs/runtime/bench/README.md: what each number means and how to run it.
